summary: Mobility is returning to near‑pre‑pandemic levels with the MF‑Index at 84 and PT ridership exceeding historic annual totals. Fuel savings remain substantial, but high fuel prices and uneven WFH adoption across sectors pose emerging risks. Targeted policy tweaks can lock in the gains while mitigating sectoral imbalances.

signals.detail: Weekly fuel savings of 35.7 million litres represent 42 % of the MCO peak, confirming that the extended WFH regime continues to curb consumption. The savings are amplified by high fuel prices (RON95 RM 3.77/L), which discourage discretionary travel. Maintaining these savings will require complementary demand‑management measures as prices stabilise.

Daily public‑transport trips reached 1,494,224, projecting an annual volume of roughly 545 million trips—above the 2019 baseline of 522 million. This indicates a robust modal shift back to PT, likely driven by congestion concerns and fuel cost pressures. Continued service reliability and fare stability will be critical to sustain this upward trend.

Retail & Services, Logistics, and Construction sectors show mobility scores of 85‑95 with WFH rates below 15 %, exposing them to higher congestion and emissions risk. Their high mobility could erode the fuel‑saving gains if not managed. Monitoring sector‑specific travel patterns will help pre‑empt economic disruptions linked to transport bottlenecks.

WFH adoption varies sharply—from 60 % in Public & GLCs to just 5 % in Construction—creating unequal exposure to fuel price shocks and traffic externalities. The disparity suggests that current policies favour certain employment groups. Introducing flexible‑hour incentives for low‑WFH sectors can improve equity and overall system resilience.

Sustained PT usage and significant fuel savings point to a durable shift away from private car dependence. However, persistently high fuel prices could trigger a rebound to private vehicles if PT affordability declines. Embedding long‑term fare subsidies and expanding feeder services will reinforce the modal transition.

recommendation: Introduce sector‑targeted flexible‑working incentives for Retail, Logistics and Construction to lift WFH adoption to at least 20 % by Q4 2027, while expanding PT capacity and capping fare hikes to keep ridership growth above 5 % annually. Simultaneously, maintain a modest fuel price differential to preserve weekly savings of 35 million litres and set a national target of a 5 % reduction in weekly fuel consumption by end‑2027.
